Why is your phone
bill so expensive?

lines.text: Phone plans got cheaper. The taxes on them hit a record.
lines.say: Phone plans got cheaper. The taxes on them hit a record.

lines.text: The Tax Foundation's 2026 study says a record 28.8% of a typical bill is taxes and fees.
lines.say: The Tax Foundation's twenty twenty-six study says a record twenty-eight point eight percent of a typical bill is taxes and fees.
That share was eighteen point six percent in twenty sixteen.

lines.text: Meanwhile, the average carrier charge per line fell from $50.64 to $33.14 a month over about two decades.
lines.say: Meanwhile, the average carrier charge per line fell from about fifty-one dollars to thirty-three over two decades.

lines.text: On a four-line, $100-a-month plan, that's about $345 a year in taxes and fees.
lines.say: On a four-line, hundred-dollar plan, that's about three hundred forty-five dollars a year in taxes and fees.

lines.text: In the study, 14.4% is the federal Universal Service Fund; state and local add about the same.
lines.say: In the study, fourteen point four percent is the federal Universal Service Fund; state and local add about the same.

lines.text: Verizon bid $45.5 billion for C-band spectrum in 2021, then spent $17 billion on capital projects in 2025.
lines.say: Verizon bid forty-five point five billion dollars for C-band spectrum in twenty twenty-one, then spent seventeen billion on capital projects in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: So the plan got cheaper. The stuff stacked on top hit a record.

post.title: Phone Service Got Cheaper. Why Do Taxes Hit a Record?
post.ig:
Phone service got cheaper. The taxes on it hit a record.
A record 28.8% of a typical wireless bill is taxes, fees and surcharges (Tax Foundation, 2026).
The average charge per line fell from $50.64 to $33.14 a month over about two decades.
A four-line, $100/month plan pays about $345 a year in taxes and fees.
Verizon bid $45.5B in the FCC's 2021 C-band auction and spent $17.0B on capex in 2025.
Sources: Tax Foundation, FCC, Verizon.
News and education, not financial advice.
